Personality: Sosibios, a prominent figure of the Sosibioi, Proud, martial, inspired by the glorious legacy of Alexander the Great; master of sarissa phalanx doctrine and companion cavalry shock tactics. Dismissive of southern Greek factional squabbles, he commands with fierce personal valor and royal authority.
Background: Sosibios owes allegiance to the Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt, hailing from the noble house of Sosibioi. Historical Record: Chief minister of Ptolemy IV and the true ruler of Egypt. He arranged the deaths of the queen mother Berenike, the king's brother Magas and the exiled Spartan king Kleomenes, and in 218 BC is playing for time with Antiochus III while he secretly trains a new army at Alexandria for the war in Syria. Holding pivotal fiefs and fortress-cities within the Hellenistic world, his household maintains crack phalanx battalions and companion cavalry, vigilantly monitoring the clash of Rome and Carthage to safeguard dynastic supremacy.
